paragraphs: In Lewisham, children who cannot live at home are cared for by the council's own fostering service or by independent agencies such as the services shown above. Fostering for the council means caring for Lewisham children with its social workers alongside you, usually close to their schools and families; an agency assesses, trains and supervises its own carers and takes children placed by councils, Lewisham among them.

The council's corporate parenting strategy for 2025 to 2028 shows why local carers matter. Lewisham looked after 439 children on 31 March 2025, 45 of them unaccompanied young people seeking asylum. Only 147 of them, a third, were living in the borough, and 79 were placed more than 20 miles from home. In April 2025, 32% of children in care were in a Lewisham foster home; the strategy's aim is 40%, by expanding the council's own pool of carers. When it opened its Fostering Hub, a single home for recruitment, training and support groups, the council linked it to a priority campaign to recruit 30 new foster carers in the year.

Lewisham says it is urgently looking for carers for children with complex and developmental needs. It also needs emergency, short-term, long-term and parent and baby carers, two-adult households for teenagers, and larger homes for sibling groups of two to six. You need to be 21 or over, with no upper age limit, single or in a couple, and to have a spare bedroom for each child over five; working full time is possible if your hours are flexible.

Approval takes up to eight months: a first contact, a home visit, checks and the three-day Skills to Foster course, an assessment with a social worker, then the fostering panel. Council carers have a supervising social worker, support groups, a mentoring scheme, access to child mental health services, a personal development plan with trauma-informed training, paid membership of the Fostering Network, and up to two weeks' break after a year caring for the same child. We do not yet have a Lewisham allowance page, so ask the council and two or three of the agencies above what they pay and how they support carers. If you live near the borough's edge, the Southwark, Greenwich, Bromley and Lambeth pages list more services.

sources.title: Lewisham Council opens new Fostering Hub in celebration with local foster carers (Lewisham Council)
